facts.statement: The scientific name of the genus is Paraetmopterus.
The genus Paraetmopterus was described by Adnet in 2006.
Paraetmopterus is an extinct genus of sharks belonging to the family Etmopteridae.
facts.quote: Paraetmopterus is an extinct genus of sharks in the family Etmopteridae.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is P. nolfi, which lived in France during the middle Eocene.
facts.quote: the type species is P. nolfi, which existed during the middle Eocene of France.

facts.statement: A species named P. horvathi, which lived in Slovakia during the Miocene, was described by Underwood and Schlögl in 2013.
facts.quote: A new species, P. horvathi, which existed in what is now Slovakia during the Miocene epoch, was described by Charlie J. Underwood and Jan Schlögl in 2013

facts.statement: The species P. horvathi was later moved to the separate genus Palaeocentroscymnus.
facts.quote: however, this species was subsequently transferred to the separate genus Palaeocentroscymnus.

facts.statement: The parent group of Paraetmopterus is the family Etmopteridae.
Paraetmopterus belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
The genus Paraetmopterus lived from 48.07 to 37.71 million years ago, spanning the Lutetian to Bartonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Lutetian to Bartonian (48.07 to 37.71 million years ago)
